exercise2.prompt: What Dirty Data Looks Like: A dirt report

hiddenCases.name: spaces alone count as blank, not as a bad number
a name seen three times repeats twice

exercise2.hint: Keep a set of names seen so far. For each row: if score.strip() == "" it is blank; elif not score.strip().isdigit() it is not a number; and if the name is already in the set it is a repeat.

questions.prompt: What makes dirty data dangerous rather than merely annoying?
choices: Nothing raises — the summary is simply wrong
questions.explain: A crash tells you where to look. A wrong average looks exactly like a right one.

questions.prompt: Which of these are the common problems in a real data file?
questions.explain: Sorting is a property of the file, not a fault in it. The other three change your answer without telling you.

questions.prompt: What is a quick way to see the variety in a column?
questions.explain: A set collapses the column to its distinct values, which is where "Maths", "maths" and "MATHS" become visible as three things.
Adding strings joins them. That is why a text column can be "totalled" without any error.
